2027-02-11.title: First Thursday of the Great Fast
2027-02-11.readTitle: Readings of the day (First Set; mapped from the official calendar, verify locally)
readings: The sin of our first parents
2027-02-11.alt: Season of the Great Fast (Sauma Ramba). In the Latin calendar 11 February is Our Lady of Lourdes, the World Day of the Sick.
2027-02-11.verse: But strive first for the kingdom of God and his righteousness, and all these things will be given to you as well.
theo: The serpent's first words are a question that twists God's command: “Did God say, ‘You shall not eat from any tree in the garden’?” Then comes the lie: “You will not die; for God knows that when you eat of it your eyes will be opened, and you will be like God, knowing good and evil.” At the root of the first sin is suspicion: the idea that God is holding something back from us, that he is a rival and not a Father. The eyes are opened, but all they see is nakedness and shame. Then, in the evening breeze, God comes looking: “But the Lord God called to the man, and said to him, “Where are you?”” God knows where Adam is. The question is an invitation to come out. Adam answers with fear, “I was afraid, because I was naked; and I hid myself”, and then with blame: “The woman whom you gave to be with me, she gave me fruit from the tree, and I ate.” The woman blames the serpent. Paul draws the conclusion for every human being: “There is no one who is righteous, not even one”, so that “every mouth may be silenced”, for “through the law comes the knowledge of sin.” The Great Fast begins in honesty: to stop hiding and stop blaming, and to answer God's question with the truth.

Joshua's people are about to enter unknown ground. The ark of the covenant goes ahead of them, carried by the priests, “so that you may know the way you should go, for you have not passed this way before.” Joshua tells them: “Sanctify yourselves; for tomorrow the LORD will do wonders among you.” God goes first into the river. In the Gospel Jesus speaks to the anxiety that began in Eden: “do not worry about your life, what you will eat or what you will drink, or about your body, what you will wear.” “Look at the birds of the air; they neither sow nor reap nor gather into barns, and yet your heavenly Father feeds them.” “Consider the lilies of the field.” In a season of fasting these words land differently. We eat less, and discover that the Father still feeds us. Worry is the old suspicion of the garden, the fear that God will not provide. Jesus answers it with an order of priorities: “But strive first for the kingdom of God and his righteousness, and all these things will be given to you as well.” Today, as the Latin Church remembers Our Lady of Lourdes and prays for the sick, let us bring to God the worries of the sick and of those who care for them.
outline: Ask: what worry woke you up this week?
Suspicion, hiding and blame; God comes looking.
The ark goes first into the river.
Point 3 · Strive first for the kingdom
The birds, the lilies, and the fast that teaches trust.
“But strive first for the kingdom of God and his righteousness.”
live: Tonight, before sleeping, answer God honestly: where am I? Plan your Lenten confession.
Write down one worry and leave it before a crucifix or an image of Our Lady.
2027-02-11.prayer: Lord God, you came looking for Adam in the garden and you still call us: where are you? Free us from the suspicion that you are not good, from hiding and from blaming others. Go before us like the ark into the river, teach us through this fast to trust your care, and help us strive first for your kingdom. Comfort the sick and all who are anxious. Amen.
altar: At the Holy Qurbana the Father gives us our daily bread in its fullest sense, the Body of his Son. We need not worry; he provides.

quick: Sin began with suspicion; God still asks: where are you?
God goes before us like the ark into the river.
Strive first for the kingdom; the Father knows what you need.
2027-02-11.action: Write down your biggest worry and hand it to God in prayer.
2027-02-11.question: Where am I hiding from God?

family.explain: Jesus says: look at the birds. They do not have kitchens or shops, but God feeds them. Look at the flowers. They do not sew clothes, but God makes them beautiful. You are worth much more to God than birds and flowers! So do not worry. Put God first.
family.intention: We pray for sick people and for those who care for them.
family.ask: Ask: “What is one thing we are worried about? Let us give it to God together.”

illus: A mother in Thodupuzha lay awake every night worrying about her son working in the Gulf. At the start of the Great Fast she began a small practice: each night she wrote her worry on a slip of paper and dropped it into a box placed before the image of Our Lady. By Easter the box was full. She laughed and told her neighbour: I gave the box the night shift. My son still has problems, but now I sleep, and I pray better in the morning.

pm.open: Lord God, you call us by name: where are you? Here we are, Lord. Amen.
share: Where are you? (Genesis 3:9). Where am I hiding from God?
Sanctify yourselves; for tomorrow the LORD will do wonders among you (Joshua 3:5). How am I preparing for what God wants to do?
Strive first for the kingdom of God (Matthew 6:33). What comes first in my life?
pm.resp: Lord, we trust in your care.
interc: For the Church, that she may proclaim God's providence.
For the sick, through the prayers of Our Lady of Lourdes.
For those overwhelmed by worry about money, work or children.
For our group, that we may seek first the kingdom.
pm.close: Father, you feed the birds and clothe the lilies. Free us from anxiety, forgive our hiding, and teach us to seek your kingdom first. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear friends, the first sin began with a suspicion: that God was holding something back. Adam and Eve ate, their eyes were opened, and they hid. Then God came looking: where are you? (Genesis 3:9). He still asks that question, not to shame us, but to call us out of hiding.

Adam blamed the woman, and the woman blamed the serpent. Paul says that no one is righteous, not even one. The Great Fast begins when we stop blaming and say honestly: Lord, here I am, a sinner in need of you.

Joshua tells the people: sanctify yourselves; for tomorrow the LORD will do wonders among you (Joshua 3:5). The ark of God goes first into the river. And Jesus tells us not to worry about food and clothing: look at the birds of the air; consider the lilies of the field.

When we fast we eat less, and we find that the Father still feeds us. So let us strive first for the kingdom of God and his righteousness, and all these things will be given to us as well (Matthew 6:33). Amen.
kids: Children, God feeds the little birds and dresses the flowers in beautiful colours. He loves you even more! When you are worried, tell Jesus about it and trust him.

intro: Theme: “But strive first for the kingdom of God and his righteousness.”
God's question in the garden, the ark that goes ahead into the river, and the trust that fasting teaches.

q: But the Lord God called to the man, and said to him, “Where are you?”
For the Son of Man came to seek out and to save the lost.
points.apply: Make a careful examination of conscience tonight and plan your Lenten confession.

q: Then Joshua said to the people, “Sanctify yourselves; for tomorrow the LORD will do wonders among you.”
Pursue peace with everyone, and the holiness without which no one will see the Lord.
points.apply: Choose one habit to give up this Lent as preparation for what God will do.

q: Cast your burden on the LORD, and he will sustain you; he will never permit the righteous to be moved.
But strive first for the kingdom of God and his righteousness, and all these things will be given to you as well.
points.apply: Each morning this week, name one worry and hand it to God before you begin work.

concl: God calls us out of hiding and goes ahead of us into the river.
Let the fast teach us to trust: the Father knows what we need.
2027-02-11.resolve: Go to confession during the first weeks of the Great Fast.
